pool.text: Alfonso I of Aragon conquered Zaragoza, making it the kingdom's capital.
A bubonic plague outbreak devastated Zaragoza's inhabitants.
Archduke Charles was proclaimed King of Aragon in Zaragoza.
Bourbon forces under the Duke of Orléans entered Zaragoza.
A Bourbon defeat near Zaragoza allowed Archduke Charles to return briefly.
Bread price riots, known as the motín de los broqueleros, erupted.
General Military Academy re-established in Zaragoza by José Enrique Varela.
Joint US‑Spain air base was installed in Zaragoza.
Zaragoza declared a Pole for Industrial Development, sparking rapid growth.
Hotel Corona de Aragón fire killed at least 80 people.
ETA bombing of Zaragoza barracks resulted in eleven deaths.
Zaragoza football club captured the Copa del Rey title.
Zaragoza football club won the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup.
Zaragoza football club secured another Copa del Rey victory.
AVE high‑speed rail began serving Zaragoza in December.
El Canal de Aguas Bravas artificial whitewater course was built for Expo.
Zaragoza airport freight traffic surpassed Barcelona El Prat.
Zaragoza became a Festival of International Tourist Interest.
Zaragoza's population reached 699,007, ranking fourth in Spain.
Zaragoza will host the ITSF World Cup and Championships.
